full_judgment: 18. Let us now turn to section 34 which deals with taking over of a waqf estate by the Administrator of Waqf overriding the terms of the Waqf deed. Here again the contention advanced in support of the Rule is that even if the impugned order is considered to be a taking over by the Administrator of the Waqfs under section 34, and not a removal of mutwalli under section 32, the taking Over should be held-illegal for non compliance with the relevant provisions of the Ordinance. Section 34 provides, "Notwithstanding anything contained elsewhere in this Ordinance or in any other law for the time being in force or in any decree Or any deed or instrument the Administrator may by notification in the official Gazette, take over and assume the administration, control, management and maintenance of any waqf property, including any shrine, dargah, imambarah or Other religious institution appertaining to such waqf property." Sub-section (3) further provides that the Administrator may manage the waqf property, thus taken over, through any officer subordinate to him or by an agent or official mutwalli or if he considers necessary, by appointing a managing committee in the case of a shrine, dargah, imambara and other religious institution. Sub-section (4) provides that if a managing committee is appointed, the mutwalli of the waqf property concerned shall be made a member.
